cover letter
Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training.
Master's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training.
Experience working directly with marine mammals in human care.
Experience acquiring and processing psychoacoustic data.

Under the general direction of Principal Researcher Dr. Reichmuth, the successful candidate will apply acquired skills and knowledge of pinniped behavior, sensory physiology, and animal training and handling techniques to support ongoing bioacoustic and psychoacoustic research projects at Long Marine Laboratory.
Selected candidate will be required to pass a pre-employment criminal history background check.
Selected candidate must pass the employment misconduct disclosure process.
Enrollment and completion of the UCSC OHSS and UCSC IACUC training is required within 2 weeks of hire.
The selected candidate will be required to work all scheduled hours on-site.

Employees whose positions are designated as Category 1 or Category 2 for occupational exposure to blood or other potentially infectious materials (OPIM) must receive the Hepatitis B vaccination or sign a Hepatitis B vaccination declination statement. Initial and annual Bloodborne Pathogens training is also required.
Selected candidate will be required to complete training within established time frames as directed including UC compliance training.

The University of California has implemented a Vaccination Policy covering all employees. Employees, including new hires, are required to comply with any applicable policies relating to the University of California vaccine program.

Per the Child Abuse and Neglect Reporting Act (CANRA), this position has been identified as a Mandated Reporter. The selected candidate will be required to report known or suspected child abuse or neglect as defined by CANRA and will be required to sign a Statement Acknowledging Requirement to Report Child Abuse prior to commencing employment. CANRA Penal Codes, and related definitions, requirements, and responsibilities may be obtained here.
Ability to complete in-house core training program and animal welfare training.
Ability to safely perform the physical requirements necessary to move light to moderate objects up to 60 lbs., with or without accommodation.
Ability to teach in-house laboratory protocols to lab staff.
Ability to work occasional evenings and weekends as directed.
Strong attention to detail and strong organizational skills.
Ability to wear proper safety attire (long pants, closed-toe shoes, etc.) and personal protective equipment common in a laboratory setting.
Strong research and analytical skills.
Strong communication skills with research partners and project team members.
Proven ability to work independently and with a team.
Demonstrated ability to meet strict deadlines with minimal supervision.
Strong written communication skills including peer-reviewed publication record.
Ability to exercise flexibility, initiative, good judgment, and discretion.
